thread:
zoe: FYI we merged the keystore RBAC split last night and early this morning EU ingress started intermittently failing mTLS handshakes. Seeing proxy 5xx spikes and keystore logs show denies. Anyone on?

liam: I noticed a small surge in client TLS failures around 02:15 UTC, thought it was a noisy test. Which principal is denied?

zoe: keystore logs show the decrypt path returning DENY because the RoleBinding didn't include the explicit service-account subject in eu-west-1 cluster. sample: 
```
2026-04-02T02:16:13Z keystore-0 INFO auth: principal=svc-ingress.eu-west-1 check=can_decrypt result=DENY reason=subject-not-in-rolebinding
2026-04-02T02:16:13Z proxy-12 WARN tls: handshake failed client=svc-api.eu, error=handshake_denied stage=unwrap-key
```

harpreet: That makes sense; our refactor introduced a cluster-local binding generation step and a template bug skipped SA subjects when cluster.labels.region=="eu". Wasn't caught by CI because the RBAC CI only validates YAML syntax.

ops-oncall: I can patch the RoleBinding now. Before patching, we should collect artifacts: kube-audit entry for the RoleBinding apply (to see when change propagated), full keystore logs, and `kubectl get rolebinding -n infra keystore-eu -o yaml`. Also capture peer_cert SHA and SNI from the proxy logs for failed handshakes.

liam: grabbing proxy logs and will grep for peer_cert_sha256. Quick helper: 
```
kubectl -n eu logs proxy-12 --since=20m | grep peer_cert_sha256 | head -n 5
```

zoe: KMS audit doesn't show decrypt calls for the proxy principal in EU. This matches the early-deny behavior we added to save KMS QPS; keystore returns DENY without calling KMS if RBAC check fails. That is why the audit sink is empty.

harpreet: Good to know. But we should also ensure we don't swallow telemetry: even when RBAC denies early, emit an audit record that flows to KMS/audit-sink so incident analysis is possible.

ops-oncall: Rolling a narrow fix to add the missing SA subjects in eu cluster now. Commands I'm running: 
```
# patch rolebinding to re-add SA subjects
kubectl --context=eu-west-1 -n infra apply -f /manifests/keystore/rolebinding-eu-patch.yaml
kubectl rollout restart deploy/keystore -n infra
```

keystore-bot: Created debug trace id dbg-20260402-0217 for keystore pods. Use this id to surface rbac_eval_trace and keystore_cache_hit in logs.

~5 minutes later~

liam: After patching, handshake failures dropped from 2.3% -> 0.1% for eu region. Good.

zoe: Follow-ups: 1) fix the RBAC template bug and add explicit SA subjects per-region rather than depending on group expansion, 2) add a canary decrypt gate to RBAC pipeline that runs in-cluster once bindings are applied (job attempts a simple decrypt as svc-proxy principal), 3) change keystore to emit an audit stub when early-deny happens containing principal, reason, sni, peer_cert_sha256, and request_id so these show up in our audit-sink even if KMS wasn't called.

harpreet: I'll open the PR to fix template and add unit tests to render bindings for all regions. Also adding a small integration test in the RBAC pipeline: after apply, run `kubectl run` as the target SA and call the canary endpoint.

ops-oncall: Also recommend a short-term alert: if mtls_handshake_denied_total{region=\"eu\"} > 5 for 5m -> page. Runbook step: check `kubectl get rolebinding -n infra keystore-* -o wide` and `kubectl logs deploy/keystore -n infra | grep rbac_eval_trace`.

zoe: Priors: ensure kube-audit policy captures RoleBinding change events with verb=update/create and include objectRef. We had that but need to make sure audit logs are forwarded to long-term storage for 90 days.

keystore-bot: Note: will add structured fields `rbac_eval_trace`, `keystore_cache_hit`, and `audit_stub_id` to keystore logs in next release.

liam: One additional idea: add a preflight step in the manifest deployment job that validates subjects by querying the cluster API after apply and failing the rollout if expected SA subjects are missing. Prevents drift due to templating bugs.

zoe: Agree. Assigning actions: harpreet -> PR for template fix + RBAC tests, liam -> canary decrypt runner + preflight check in pipeline, ops-oncall -> update runbook and alert rule, security-bot -> attach incident INC-2026-060 to PR and remind to include timeline.

security-bot: Incident INC-2026-060 created and linked. Severity: P2. Reminder to include customer-impact assessment if outage >5 minutes.

zoe: Thanks all. We'll run a short blameless postmortem focusing on pipeline preflight and telemetry gaps if we see recurrence.
